question: The systems $2x+y=4$, $x+3y=7$ and $2u+v=5$, $u+3v=0$ have the same coefficient matrix. Find the inverse of this common coefficient matrix, use it to solve both systems, and hence establish that the sum of their solution vectors solves the system obtained by adding the corresponding right-hand sides.
explanation:
Common coefficient matrix
The common coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Its determinant is
$$|A|=2(3)-1(1)=5\neq0$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

Solution of the first system
For the first system,
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}4\\7\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\7\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}12-7\\-4+14\end{bmatrix}$$
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
For the second system,
$$\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}5\\0\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\0\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}15\\-5\end{bmatrix}$$
$$\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification of the combined system
The sum of the solution vectors is
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
The sum of the right-hand-side vectors is
$$\begin{bmatrix}4\\7\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}9\\7\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$A\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}9\\7\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore, the sum vector $\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}$ solves the combined system $2X+Y=9$ and $X+3Y=7$, as required.

options.A: $A^{-1}=\frac15\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$; $(x,y)=(1,2)$ and $(u,v)=(3,-1)$; their sum is $(4,1)$, which solves $2X+Y=9$ and $X+3Y=7$
options.B: $A^{-1}=\frac15\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}$; $(x,y)=(1,2)$ and $(u,v)=(3,-1)$; their sum $(4,1)$ solves the combined system
options.C: $A^{-1}=\frac15\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$; $(x,y)=(2,1)$ and $(u,v)=(3,-1)$; their sum $(5,0)$ solves the combined system
